name: Nathan Hovekamp
reasoning: EVIDENCE CAVEAT: both Planning Commission minutes cited here carry a printed disclaimer that they are "DERIVED FROM AN AUTOMATED TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE AND HAVE BEEN SUMMARIZED THROUGH AN AUTOMATED PROCESS" and "may not capture the full context or nuances" — the formal motion language is reliable, but no verbatim quote is published from them for that reason. Hovekamp sits on the Deschutes County Planning Commission, which is where these recorded land-use actions are (a different body from the park board seat this record is attached to). At the May 8, 2025 PC meeting Hovekamp personally moved to close deliberations on the Clear and Objective Housing Text Amendments - Goal 5 package and to recommend approval of the language as drafted (seconded by Vice Chair Altman). That package converts discretionary standards in the Wildlife Area, Sensitive Bird and Mammal Habitat and Landscape Management combining zones into objective ones and creates a streamlined approval path running parallel to the existing discretionary path, while (per staff and legal counsel) leaving the county's acknowledged Goal 5 inventories and impact areas unchanged; his motion carried notwithstanding Central Oregon LandWatch's request for a fresh ESEE analysis. At the April 24, 2025 hearing on the same package he asked about using a qualified biologist in the process to address ODFW's concern about losing site-specific analysis. This matches chair 3, 'Apply consistent environmental standards while giving developers reasonable flexibility on implementation' - he kept the substantive environmental standards and biological review in play while affirmatively moving approval of the objective, flexible pathway. It is not chair 1 ('Require significant green space, tree preservation, and environmental review before approving any development') or chair 2 ('require developers to fully offset any environmental impact'), because he moved to approve removing the discretionary exception process rather than to add review or offset duties; and it is not chair 4 or 5, because the amendments preserved the underlying Goal 5 protections rather than substituting fees for on-site preservation.
quote_deidentified: Moved to close deliberations on the county's clear-and-objective housing text amendments for Goal 5 resources and to recommend approval of the language as drafted; at the earlier hearing on the same package, asked about the potential use of a qualified biologist in the process to address the state wildlife agency's concern about losing site-specific analysis.

name: Nathan Hovekamp
reasoning: At the Sept. 23, 2025 BPRD board meeting Hovekamp voted against both requests for 20-year property-tax exemptions under the City of Bend's Income Qualified Tax Exemption program - Cascade Landing (98 low-income units, 20-year impact to the district calculated at $792,848) and Verde Pines (128 low-income units, roughly $556,445) - and each motion failed 2-2, with Schneider and Schoen in favor and Hovekamp and Owens opposed. At the March 17, 2026 joint meeting with Bend City Council the minutes record his own rationale: Hovekamp "raised issues of fairness around burdens placed on residents and taxpayers supporting new housing" and "would like to continue to support affordable housing, but did not feel it should or needs to be at the expense of providing other services." (In the same passage he also relayed BPRD survey findings that constituents oppose tax exemptions; that is reported constituent opinion, not his own position, and is not treated as load-bearing here.) That is chair 3, 'Keep the current tax system mostly as-is with small adjustments to close unfair loopholes' - he defends the existing tax base against carve-outs specifically so that services stay funded. It is not chair 1 or 2, since he never proposes raising taxes on wealthy people or large companies; and not chair 4 or 5, since he expressly refuses to trade away revenue and the services it buys. These were substantive votes on exemption applications with a stated rationale, not a procedural referral of a bond or levy to voters.
quote_deidentified: Voted against two twenty-year property-tax exemption requests for low-income housing developments, and later explained that residents and taxpayers were being asked to carry an unfair share of the burden of supporting new housing; would like to continue to support affordable housing but did not feel it should or needs to be at the expense of providing other services.

name: Cary Schneider
reasoning: In his own May 2025 Deschutes County voters' pamphlet statement Schneider commits to maximizing the impact of tax dollars by balancing reinvestment in existing parks with allocating appropriate resources for future growth, and to connecting trails and increasing park, green space and recreation-service capacity through thoughtful planning. His recorded actions match: on Sept. 23, 2025 he voted in favor of both 20-year property-tax exemptions for the 98-unit Cascade Landing and 128-unit Verde Pines low-income housing projects (each failed 2-2), accepting a revenue cost to his own district so the housing could proceed; and at the March 17, 2026 joint meeting with City Council he acknowledged the topic was difficult but proposed non-monetary alternatives - allocating some Transient Room Tax funds to support BPRD, waiving BPRD permit fees, or reducing the City's Transportation Fee - to free up district funds to support housing. That is chair 3, 'Plan proactively - invest in infrastructure ahead of growth to support responsible expansion.' It is not chair 2 ('Allow growth only where existing infrastructure can support it; slow approvals until capacity catches up'), because he voted to let the development proceed rather than condition it on capacity catching up; and not chair 4 ('Streamline permitting, reduce fees, and actively recruit development to grow the tax base'), because he sought mechanisms to keep the park district financially whole rather than treating fee reduction as the goal, and never argued for recruiting development.
quote_text: Maximize the impact of tax dollars by balancing the reinvestment in our existing parks and recreation facilities along with allocating appropriate resources for future growth.

name: Deb Schoen
reasoning: Schoen's own May 2025 Deschutes County voters' pamphlet statement says she will prioritize planning for growth, alongside fiscal responsibility and equitable access. Her recorded actions match: at the Sept. 23, 2025 BPRD meeting she made both motions to approve 20-year property-tax exemptions for the 98-unit Cascade Landing and 128-unit Verde Pines low-income housing developments and voted for both (each failed 2-2), accepting a calculated revenue loss to her own district so the housing could be built; and on July 21, 2026 she presented the City of Bend shared framework to the board as recognizing mutual benefit by supporting both housing and parks while avoiding actions that could compromise either agency's ability to deliver essential services, anticipating future work on SDC waivers, permitting, urban renewal impacts and transportation system fees. That is chair 3, 'Plan proactively - invest in infrastructure ahead of growth to support responsible expansion.' It is not chair 2, because she voted to enable the development rather than slow approvals until capacity caught up; and not chair 4, because she pairs support for new development with protecting the district's service delivery rather than reducing fees to grow the tax base.
quote_text: I will prioritize planning for growth, exercising fiscal responsibility, and ensuring equitable access to nature and programs for our community by maximizing participation in decision-making, addressing barriers, and advocating for sustainable practices in our parks.
